title: THE TEMPERATURE LADDER -- one velocity scale (the triad's sigma), three temperatures (phase / free-dust / baryonic gas), stated with the numbers and the honest rung census
question: G151: state the framework's three temperatures -- (a) the equilibrium phase T = m sigma^2/k_B (9.17 K at 5 keV, mass-free in T/m); (b) the free dust's kinetic T (2.04e-5 K at z = 3, falling as (1+z)^2); (c) the baryonic gas T = mu m_p sigma^2/k_B at the same sigma (the cluster 3.6 keV-class); the ladder's ratios; the bookkeeping statement; which rungs are observable; the verdicts.

references.G116: T/m = sigma^2/k_B mass-free (1.83-2.01 mK/eV); T_phase(5 keV) = 9.17 K; free dust T(z=3) = 2.0436e-5 K (1.2796e-6 K z=0); decoupling ratio 4.5e+05x; sigma = 119.209 km/s
references.G093: the free-dust coldness: v_th(z=0) = 0.0548 km/s, v_th(z=3) = 0.219 km/s (3.3 keV), lambda_fs 0.50-0.82 Mpc, c_s^2(z=3) = 5.34e-13/1.79e-13 vs L194 1e-9 (1872x) / L224 1.1e-11 (61x); V4 non-claims (no direct-detection coupling, THEORY.md 8)

references.G109: cross-instrument sigma: sigma_gal/sigma_gas,1D median 0.998, log10 rms 0.0621 dex (11 clusters); kTvir median 6.17 keV <-> sigma_1d = 992 km/s; mu = 0.6

references.G075: clusters under the triad: T_X,pred = mu m_p sigma^2/(2 k_B) median T_pred/T_obs = 0.28 (canonical) / 0.31 (alt) -- the ICM ~3.6x hotter than the /2-convention baryon floor; kTvir per cluster (Eckert+17 Table 1), median 6.17 keV

V1_the_ladder_complete.statement: THE LADDER WITH THE NUMBERS: (a) T = m sigma^2/k_B = 9.17 K at m = 5 keV, sigma = 119.2 km/s (T/m = 1.835 mK/eV mass-free, band 1.83-2.01); (b) T = m v_th^2/k_B = 2.04e-5 K at z = 3 (1.28e-6 K at z = 0), falling as (1+z)^2 (ratio 16 exactly); (c) T = mu m_p sigma^2/k_B = 89.0 eV at the same sigma; 3.68 keV at the cluster triad sigma (A85 M_b(R500) = 1.109e14 Msun -> 766.1 km/s; 4.10 keV at the G008-registered 809 km/s; 3.6 keV <-> 758 km/s); observed kTvir median 6.17 keV. Ratios on the committed numbers: a/b = 4.49e5 (the registered 4.5e5 decoupling ratio), c/a = 1.126e5 = mu m_p/m exact, c/b = 5.06e10 (equal sigma) / 2.09e12 (cluster rung); c(A85)/a = 4.65e6. The brief's glosses corrected: c/a ~ 1e5 correct; a/b = 4.5e5 not 1e4; c/b ~ 5e10 not 1e9.

V2_the_observable_rungs.statement: EXACTLY ONE rung is instrument-reachable: (c), the baryonic gas T = mu m_p sigma^2/k_B -- X-ray/SZ kTvir, galaxy sigma, lensing M <-> T -- confirmed on the record at the 0.06-0.10 dex level (G109: sigma_gal/sigma_gas = 0.998 median, rms 0.062 dex; G095: closed-form T ratio within 1.8% at the median, 0.051-0.053 dex scatter = HSE; G075: kTvir vs the zero-parameter triad rung within a factor 1.5-1.7). Rungs (a) 9.17 K and (b) 2.04e-5 K are unobservable by the theory's own construction (no radiation, no collision, no direct-detection channel, G093 V4/THEORY.md 8); therefore NONE of the ladder's pair ratios (c/a, a/b, c/b) is measurable -- there is no instrument for 9.17 K or 2.04e-5 K, so no ratio containing them can be read.

V3_the_honest_statement.statement: THE TEMPERATURE LADDER IS A BOOKKEEPING STATEMENT, NOT A NEW OBSERVABLE. One velocity scale (the triad's sigma; T/m = sigma^2/k_B registered constant; the gas at equipartition with the same sigma) and three temperatures -- set by the mass (phase: T/m mass-free), the coupling (gas: c/a = mu m_p/m = 1.126e5 exactly), and the expansion (dust: (1+z)^2) -- organize the framework's thermodynamic ledger and add nothing measurable to it. Two of the three rungs are inert by construction: the 9.17 K phase radiates nothing and collides with nothing; the 2.04e-5 K dust leaves only a c_s^2 = 1e-13 footprint 61-1872x under the tightest registered residuals. The one rung with empirical content is the baryonic gas T = mu m_p sigma^2/k_B -- the ordinary ICM virial relation -- already confirmed at 0.06-0.10 dex (G109 cross-instrument equipartition; G095 closed form + HSE scatter 0.053 dex), and the zero-parameter cluster rung (M_b -> sigma_pred = 766-809 km/s -> 3.68-4.10 keV) sits a factor 1.5-1.7 under the observed 6.17 keV median. The ladder's ratios are identities between bookkeeping temperatures; the honest claim is that the ladder adds no observable to the theory -- it states, in one table, what the theory's temperatures are and which one the data already measure.

measured.empirical_rung: T = mu m_p sigma^2/k_B (ICM virial relation)

statement: THE TEMPERATURE LADDER: one velocity scale (the triad's sigma), three temperatures -- (a) the equilibrium phase T = m sigma^2/k_B = 9.17 K at 5 keV (T/m = 1.835 mK/eV mass-free; set by the mass); (b) the free dust T = m v_th^2/k_B = 2.04e-5 K at z = 3 falling as (1+z)^2 (set by the expansion; never equilibrates); (c) the baryonic gas T = mu m_p sigma^2/k_B = 89 eV at the same sigma, 3.6-4.1 keV at the cluster triad sigma (set by the coupling: c/a = mu m_p/m = 1.126e5 exactly), observed at kTvir = 6.17 keV median. Ratios: a/b = 4.49e5 (the registered 4.5e5 decoupling ratio), c/a = 1.126e5, c/b = 5.06e10 (equal sigma). Two rungs are observationally inert (no radiation, no collision); no ladder ratio is measurable; the one rung with empirical content is the gas temperature T = mu m_p sigma^2/k_B, already confirmed at 0.06-0.10 dex -- the ladder is bookkeeping, not a new observable.
